evidence.title: 10-K FY2025 · Item 1 · Customers
evidence.text: Our customers are hyperscale cloud providers, GPU cloud operators, original design manufacturers that build servers for those providers, and network equipment manufacturers. Our three largest end customers, each a hyperscale cloud provider, accounted for 27%, 19%, and 15% of fiscal 2025 revenue, or 61% in total, compared with 58% in fiscal 2024. We refer to them as Customer A, Customer B, and Customer C. Our backlog was approximately $3.4 billion at December 31, 2025, compared with $2.1 billion a year earlier. Most backlog is expected to ship within twelve months, but customers may reschedule or cancel orders with limited penalties.

evidence.title: 10-K FY2025 · Item 1A · Risks Related to Our Customers and Markets
evidence.text: We depend on a small number of hyperscale customers, and the loss of, or a reduction in orders from, any of them would materially reduce our revenue. Our three largest customers accounted for 61% of fiscal 2025 revenue. These customers have substantial negotiating leverage, do not commit to long-term purchase volumes, and may qualify additional suppliers, design their own optics, or change architectures. A decision by Customer A alone to shift volume to a competitor could reduce our annual revenue by more than $1 billion. Demand for our products depends on continued growth in artificial intelligence infrastructure spending, which may slow or reverse. Our growth since 2023 has been driven by hyperscaler and GPU-cloud capital spending on AI clusters. If AI adoption slows, if model efficiency improvements reduce the need for compute, if customers digest previously purchased capacity, or if financing for data center construction tightens, orders for our products could fall sharply. Our revenue fell 14% in fiscal 2020 during a prior data center digestion period. Architecture transitions, including co-packaged optics and linear-drive optics, could reduce demand for our pluggable products. Switch and GPU vendors are developing co-packaged optics that place optical engines next to the silicon. If co-packaged optics are adopted faster than we expect, demand for pluggable transceivers, which represented most of Optical Interconnect revenue in fiscal 2025, could decline before our co-packaged engines are qualified. Pricing pressure could reduce our gross margin. Average selling prices

evidence.title: 10-K FY2025 · Item 8 · Segment and Concentration Information
evidence.text: We report two segments, Optical Interconnect and Rack Systems, which our Chief Executive Officer, as chief operating decision maker, reviews based on revenue and gross profit. Operating expenses are managed on a company-wide basis and are not allocated to segments. In fiscal 2025, Customer A, Customer B, and Customer C represented 27%, 19%, and 15% of revenue, respectively, and together represented 54% of accounts receivable at December 31, 2025.

evidence.title: 10-K FY2025 · Item 1 · Government Regulation and Export Controls
evidence.text: Our products and technology are subject to the U.S. Export Administration Regulations. Since 2023, U.S. rules restricting exports of advanced computing items to China and certain other countries have reduced our sales to customers in those countries. Revenue from customers headquartered in China was 3% of fiscal 2025 revenue, compared with 9% in fiscal 2023. We must screen customers against the Entity List and other restricted-party lists, and we may need licenses to ship certain products. We are subject to tariffs on components imported from China and to customs rules in every country where we manufacture. Our Rack Systems products use coolant fluids and refrigerants that are subject to evolving environmental regulation, including restrictions on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances in the European Union and several U.S. states and phase-down rules for certain hydrofluorocarbon refrigerants. We are also subject to conflict-minerals disclosure rules, the EU RoHS and REACH directives, and data privacy laws that apply to the telemetry our racks report.

evidence.title: 10-K FY2025 · Item 1A · Legal, Regulatory, and Compliance Risks
evidence.text: Export controls and trade restrictions have reduced, and may further reduce, our ability to sell to certain customers. U.S. export controls on advanced computing items and related technology, and any future restrictions on optical components, could prevent sales to customers in China and other countries, require licenses that may be denied, or prompt foreign governments to retaliate against U.S. suppliers. Violations of export control laws can result in significant penalties. Tariffs and changes in trade policy could increase our costs. We import components into the United States, Malaysia, Thailand, and Mexico. New or increased tariffs, including those affecting goods assembled in Mexico, could raise our costs or make our products less competitive. Environmental regulation of coolant fluids could require product changes. Restrictions on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and certain refrigerants could limit the fluids our Rack Systems products use and require costly redesign or requalification. Cybersecurity incidents could disrupt our operations or expose customer data. Our racks report operating telemetry, and our systems hold customer roadmaps and designs. A cyberattack on us or our suppliers could interrupt manufacturing, compromise data, or allow tampering with product firmware.

evidence.title: 10-K FY2025 · Item 9A. Controls and Procedures
evidence.text: This synthetic report includes no evaluation of disclosure controls or internal control over financial reporting, and no auditor attestation.

evidence.title: 10-K FY2025 · Item 1A. Risk Factors
evidence.text: Investing in our common stock involves risk. The risks below could materially affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, and stock price. Because this is a synthetic report, these risks are illustrative.

evidence.title: 10-K FY2025 · Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
evidence.text: Interest rate risk. Our investment portfolio consists of high-quality, short-duration securities; a 100-basis-point change in interest rates would change its fair value by approximately $6 million. Our senior notes bear a fixed rate. Foreign currency risk. Our sales are denominated in U.S. dollars, but a portion of our operating costs is denominated in Malaysian ringgit, Thai baht, Mexican pesos, and euros. A 10% strengthening of those currencies would have increased fiscal 2025 operating costs by approximately $48 million. Commodity risk. We are exposed to price changes for copper, aluminum, indium, and gallium used in our products and do not currently hedge these exposures.

evidence.title: 10-K FY2025 · Item 1C · Risk Management and Strategy
evidence.text: We maintain a cybersecurity risk management program aligned with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework. The program covers our corporate network, our manufacturing systems in Penang, Thailand, Austin, and Guadalajara, product firmware, and the telemetry service our racks use. We perform annual third-party penetration tests, assess critical suppliers, and operate a security operations center that monitors identity, endpoint, network, and cloud telemetry around the clock. We segment manufacturing networks from corporate networks and sign all product firmware. We have adopted controls for our internal use of generative AI, including inspection of prompts and responses for sensitive data on our private model endpoint, logging of AI assistant activity, and restrictions on the data that may be sent to hosted AI services. We did not identify any cybersecurity incident in fiscal 2025 that materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, our business strategy, results of operations, or financial condition.

evidence.text: ($ in millions) FY2025 FY2024 Change Optical Interconnect revenue $ 2,632.1 $ 2,041.4 +28.9% Rack Systems revenue $ 1,480.5 $ 938.7 +57.7% Total revenue $ 4,112.6 $ 2,980.1 +38.0% Optical Interconnect gross profit $ 1,232.0 $ 917.6 +34.3% Optical Interconnect gross margin 46.8% 44.9% +190 bps Rack Systems gross profit $ 462.4 $ 247.6 +86.8% Rack Systems gross margin 31.2% 26.4% +480 bps Optical Interconnect revenue increased 28.9% to $2,632.1 million, or 64% of total revenue, driven by 800G volume and the 1.6T ramp. Segment gross margin increased to 46.8% as Penang yields on 1.6T improved during the second half. Rack Systems revenue increased 57.7% to $1,480.5 million, or 36% of total revenue. Segment gross margin increased to 31.2% on manufacturing scale, partly offset by $14.2 million of warranty expense for the coupling seal field remediation program.

Unit volume growth in optical modules and the first full year of HR-series rack shipments more than offset average selling price declines of approximately 9% on comparable optical products.
